purpose: Durably cluster RFC-0002 GitHub issue learnings so future implementation slices inspect related defects, preserve no-claim boundaries, and update context or skills when repeated patterns recur.

patterns.title: GitHub issue state, closure wording, docs, wiki, and agent-context truth must remain executable and mainline-backed.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Before changing RFC-0002 truth, run the execution ledger gate and live state audit, generate the issue execution summary instead of relying on chat or ad hoc assignee filters, and generate the live cross-repo posture from the governed owner/dependency repository set rather than a hand-maintained subset. Preserve Keep-open wording for partial issues, ensure partial PR title/body text uses neutral verbs instead of GitHub auto-close keywords, ensure parent open_tracker issues carry status/tracker, and record exact PR/main/wiki/branch evidence on the owning issue. Pending final-closure and post-completion issues must carry status/blocked, not status/ready, while prerequisite RFC blockers remain open; their richer pending execution status remains in the ledger and summary. Classify every open status/blocked cross-repo RFC-0002 issue through the blocker classification contract: Core, production identity/session authority, protected runtime/deployment evidence, provider/bank/legal approval, final-closure prerequisites, and certification evidence may remain blocked; writable app-code work must move out of blocked posture and become ready or in-progress. When a partial merge changes an issue's execution posture, update the source-controlled ledger closure instruction and operator docs with the exact PR, main SHA, primary/security runs, wiki decision, and branch cleanup evidence instead of leaving older current-main references behind. If the PR-text gate fails, edit the PR body and create a fresh PR event with a source-controlled push before rerunning because Actions reruns can retain the stale pull_request payload.
nonClaimBoundaries: Issue state labels are not proof; they must point to PR, SHA, run, wiki, and branch evidence.
Slice 18 context updates do not complete RFC-0002 while implementation slices remain open.

patterns.title: Workbench and Gateway product-surface proof must be backed by route, panel, action, feedback, conversion-intent, and identity evidence.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Treat local/test caller fixtures and static Workbench or Gateway declarations as non-certifying until owner route proof, UI consumption proof, and production identity evidence are available. Runtime UI consumption must arrive through the Gateway/Workbench runtime-execution proof consumer and may clear only its named BFF-consumption blocker while preserving production identity, accessibility, canonical demo, data-product, client-publication, suitability/execution, and supported-feature blockers. Nested API route modules are inside the caller-context contract gate and must not bypass trusted-caller provenance or strict role-and-capability enforcement.
nonClaimBoundaries: Local/test caller authority fixtures are not production identity, authentication, or authorization proof.
Backend source contracts alone do not prove populated Workbench panel readiness.

patterns.title: Core, Advise, Manage, Report, Render, and Archive handoffs require owner runtime or materialization evidence before blockers clear.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Classify each downstream artifact by evidence class first: source-contract evidence can support readiness, but only accepted owner runtime receipts or owner materialization records can clear live execution, render, archive, or publication blockers. For Manage, bounded action-intake receipts may clear only the live-route blocker and must preserve action-register, rebalance, order, publication, production, and support blockers. Manage mandate runtime proof may consume source-owned temporal receipt identity only when evidence-as-of date, producer-generated time, temporal identity status, source batch fingerprint, and source-ref as-of posture reconcile; it must still preserve production trusted caller-context blockers until an IdP/session/token-claims authority exists. For Report materialization, bounded runtime receipts may clear report_evidence_pack_live_materialization_proof_missing, rendered_output_creation_missing, and archive_record_creation_missing only when accepted archived receipts are bound to exact Render and Archive owner-mainline evidence; they must preserve client-publication, production-identity, legal/retention, support, final-certification, and supported-feature blockers.
nonClaimBoundaries: Idea owns opportunity intent and evidence-pack request posture, not suitability approval, rebalance execution, report rendering, archive retention, or client publication.
Quarantined or fixture-backed outcome history is diagnostic and does not certify downstream persistence.

patterns.title: Data-product promotion and runtime trust telemetry require mesh catalog, policy, discovery, and supported-feature evidence to agree.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Use the shared supported-feature promotion evaluator and runtime trust telemetry posture instead of independent status counters or static catalog inclusion claims.
nonClaimBoundaries: Mesh policy or catalog source contracts alone do not certify data-product publication.
Runtime trust telemetry snapshots do not promote customer-facing supported features without current evidence and owner approvals.

patterns.title: Operations, security, lifecycle, migration, outbox, SLO, capacity, and disaster-recovery claims need protected or production-like attestations.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Separate contract-green local posture from protected execution evidence; do not clear capacity, lifecycle, migration, broker, DR, vulnerability, or incident-response blockers with static files, local-only probes, or stale report-only evidence. For #343/#344/#375/#797-style operations blockers, record which repository-owned controls are mainline-backed and which protected, bank, provider, environment-secret, target-database, workflow-run, approval, incident-commander, escalation, or post-incident problem-management evidence remains absent before changing status. Treat pyproject build-system roots as governed dependency posture inputs; exact runtime/dev pins are insufficient if build backend/tooling can resolve through unpinned or range-based requirements. For #807-style container findings, first remove final-image package installers, build tools, caches, and vendored metadata that are not application runtime dependencies; do not add scanner exceptions for removable installer-only artifacts, and prove the result with docker build, container image scan, and runtime smoke evidence. Link any future vulnerability exception to the platform-wide exception register with a VX-* platform identity, current platform schema ref, affected version or digest, exposure and exploitability assessments, planned remediation path, and active/no-active register status that matches the exception list; platform report-only validation remains non-certifying before promotion. Keep incident-response customer-communication and production-certification language source-safe until bank-approved communication authority, production identity, and protected operational evidence exist.
nonClaimBoundaries: Local/disposable database drills are not provider backup, PITR, failover, or production certification.
Static SLO, dashboard, lifecycle, outbox, incident-response, or dependency posture contracts are non-certifying until runtime/protected/release evidence exists.

patterns.title: AI explanation output acceptance requires attested lotus-ai execution, model provenance, retention, and lineage evidence.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Keep deterministic fallback/local AI output and static workflow-pack registration separate from live provider attestation; only signed, source-safe, retention-bound runtime execution can clear #340. When an AI runtime proof cites an actual runtime receipt, validate temporal provenance coherently: the proof artifact cannot be generated before the runtime receipt it cites, and aggregate readiness should preserve the runtime blocker or emit a source-safe provenance diagnostic instead of accepting internally inconsistent evidence.
nonClaimBoundaries: Idea does not implement lotus-ai provider execution, model approval, or provider retention authority.
Local fallback output is diagnostic and cannot certify workflow output acceptance.

patterns.title: Demo readiness, commercial proof, canonical archetypes, and full live journey claims must be implementation-backed end to end.
patterns.futureAgentRule: Treat commercial language as downstream of evidence: canonical opportunity archetypes, demo claim matrices, and live journeys must cite current implementation proof and preserve blockers where source-owner runtime evidence is absent. Treat missing work inside writable Lotus app/platform repositories as fix-forward scope, not blocked; reserve blocked posture for external or non-writable dependencies such as core-owner work that must be issue-backed.
nonClaimBoundaries: Research, blueprint language, and demo copy cannot promote unsupported features.
A single capability proof does not certify the full API, Gateway, Workbench, and downstream handoff journey.
